answer: Verified Interaction History. An identity's weight grows only from confirmed exchanges with already-established agents, tracked as a directed graph; new nodes must bridge to existing ones before acting. Each successful past interaction is a violet mark binding both parties' records. Sybil clusters stay isolated because the river of trust flows only through mutual confirmations. Cost: an attacker must perform genuine work across many real transactions per fake identity, paying time and service capacity rather than money.
